The pattern "The X has an associated Y" is typically for internal state of an object, like this:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded

For an algorithm which can be implemented by an element or not, it's more commonly done as "steps" which can be defined by various elements. Examples of this pattern:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#html-element-insertion-steps
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#html-element-removing-steps

I don't think there's anything wrong with defining an algorithm and overriding it in the style of C++ virtual functions, but I can't find examples of that style in this spec now.

That does seem odd. Here's the behavior I'm thinking about distilled:
https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=12699

I see that the spec never creates and `InvokeEvent` or fires it, where should that happen? If the event doesn't bubble then probably nobody has noticed the difference between using `currentTarget` and `target` yet, and the test looks like it won't be affected by the difference either, because the event handlers are on the direct target (`slot`) and on the shadow host.

Is the intention for HTML to fire the "interest" event, or where should that happen?

body:
> I see that the spec never creates and `InvokeEvent` or fires it, where should that happen? 

Oh that's a mistake. Fixed in [5231e73](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9841/commits/5231e734137f8e6984b943909cb40a4f6c129dad).

> If the event doesn't bubble then probably nobody has noticed the difference between using `currentTarget` and `target` yet, and the test looks like it won't be affected by the difference either, because the event handlers are on the direct target (`slot`) and on the shadow host.

Despite bubbling it's still observable due to the capturing phase, given the event is composed. Also the host is outside of the shadow boundary so it does get retargeted - but I don't know if it would be observably different with `target` vs `currentTarget`. We should probably do more testing on this. 

> Is the intention for HTML to fire the "interest" event, or where should that happen?

I think "interest" has its own `InterestEvent` constructor.

This step should not be run if either `shouldShowPopover` or `shouldHidePopover` are `true`. I could add an assert here if you feel it would clarify?

The possible states are:

 - The user has expressed an action of `showpopover`/`hidepopover`/`togglepopover` and the invokee is _not_ a popover - then the element invocation action should NOT run.
 - The user has expressed an action of `showpopover`/`hidepopover`/`togglepopover` and the invokee _is_ a popover - then the element invocation action should NOT run.
 - The action is auto and the invokee _is_ a popover, then the element invocation action should NOT run.
 - The action is auto and the invokee is _not_ a popover, then the element invocation action SHOULD run.

The various states are extensively tested: 
 - https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/invokers/interesttarget-on-popover-behavior.tentative.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
 - https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/invokers/invoketarget-on-popover-behavior.tentative.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned

AIUI `shouldHidePopover`/`shouldShowPopover` can only be true if the invokee is a popover. If the invokee is _not_ a popover but one of the popover actions was expressed, then that will be caught by the the early returns above which check the elements `is valid invoke action steps`.

body:
It's very rare that events are retargeted. I think it's only `relatedTarget`. As you point out re-targeting against `target` means it's the same element. I've confirmed this by changing the Firefox impl to retarget against `target` and it fails the existing tests. I don't think there's an alternative to retargeting against `currentTarget`. 

I've added a test which uses capturing events vs bubbling events and it passes, but it feels redundant. So ultimately I think everything we have in place is good and I'm not sure we want to do anything further here, but I'm happy to take suggestions!
